newsitem.title: UK: Brazil planning $750 million global bond - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil planning $750 million global bond - dealers.

text.p: Brazil may issue a $750 million global bond next week, syndicate managers said on Thursday.
A five- or a 10-year maturity is likely and a mandate was due to be awarded in the next few days, they said.

There is very little Brazilian sovereign paper outstanding in the Eurobond market, and no emerging market 10-year dollar bonds. Dealers said the scarcity of comparable deals was making it harder to predict the likely launch spread.
"A five-year would come inside 300 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, which is where a CVRD deal is trading," said a syndicate manager at a European bank.
"The ten-year is more difficult to predict as neither Argentina nor Mexico have such deals outstanding. Somewhere between 350 to 375 b.p. over would be likely," he said.
But the rarity value of Brazil may push spreads lower.
"Everyone is extremely interested in this because Brazil is such a rare Euromarket borrower," said a syndicate manager at a European bank.
"Competition (for the mandate) will be fierce," he said.

Brazil has been rumoured for some time to be considering a Brady bond buy-back along the lines of deals done by Mexico and the Philippines. But syndicate managers said there was no specific connection between the upcoming global and such a move.
